tools.name: get_calls
tools.description:
Get the logged calls that the current user can see, with their dates and attendees.

Each call has a `startTime`: the date and time of the call that the user gave
when they logged it. `createdAt` is when the record was created in Affinity,
not when the call took place. To select calls by the day they took place,
filter on `startTime`. The results include only the calls that the current
user has permission to see, so a count of them is not an organization total.

Calls come in id order, which is the order in which Affinity stored them, not
the order of their dates. The first page holds the calls that Affinity stored
first. To get recent calls, filter on `startTime`.

To get the calls of one company, person, or opportunity, use
get_interactions_for_entity. It returns calls newest first.

Args:
    filter_expr: Filter expression using Affinity query language. Available fields:
        - id: unique identifier for the call (operators: =)
          Example: "id=1" or "(id=1 | id=2)"
        - startTime: When the call took place (operators: >, <, >=, <=)
          Format: ISO 8601 timestamp
          Example: "startTime>=2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"
        - createdAt: When the call was created in Affinity (operators: >, <, >=, <=)
          Format: ISO 8601 timestamp
          Example: "createdAt>=2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"
        - updatedAt: When the call was last updated (operators: >, <, >=, <=)
          Format: ISO 8601 timestamp
          Example: "updatedAt<=2025-12-31T23:59:59Z"

        Date range example:
        "startTime>=2025-01-01T00:00:00Z & startTime<2025-02-01T00:00:00Z"

        Boolean logic: & (AND), | (OR), () for grouping
        Full filtering spec: https://developer.affinity.co/pages/external-api-v2/filtering

    cursor: Cursor for the next or previous page. Pass the value of
        `pagination.nextCursor` or `pagination.prevCursor` from a prior
        response. Do NOT parse or modify the cursor string.
    limit: Number of items to include in the page. Default is 20, max is 20.
        To get more calls, page through with `cursor`.

Returns:
    A dict with `data` (list of calls) and `pagination` with
    `nextCursor` / `prevCursor` strings (pass directly to the `cursor`
    param; absent when there is no such page) and `nextUrl` / `prevUrl`
    full URLs (null when there is no such page).
    Each call has `id`, `title` (null when the call has no title, "********"
    when the user cannot see it), `startTime`, `endTime` (can be null),
    `allDay`, `loggingType` (always "manual"), `creator` (an attendee, or
    null), `createdAt`, `updatedAt` (can be null), and `attendeesPreview`
    (`data`, a list of attendees, and `totalCount`). Each attendee has
    `emailAddress` and `person`, which is null when no person in Affinity
    has that address.

tools.name: get_chat_messages
tools.description:
Get the logged chat messages that the current user can see, with their dates, direction, and participants.

The API returns no message text. A user logs a chat message by hand, and the
text they enter is kept as a note on the message. get_interactions_for_entity
returns the ids of these notes. To read the text of a note, use query_notes
with filter_expr "id=<note id>".

Chat messages come newest first by `createdAt`, which is when a user logged
the message in Affinity, not when it was sent. To select messages by the
date they were sent, filter on `sentAt`.

To get the chat messages of one company, person, or opportunity, use
get_interactions_for_entity. It returns chat messages newest first by the
date they were sent.

Args:
    filter_expr: Filter expression using Affinity query language. Available fields:
        - id: unique identifier for the chat message (operators: =)
          Example: "id=1" or "(id=1 | id=2)"
        - sentAt: When the message was sent (operators: >, <, >=, <=)
          Format: ISO 8601 timestamp
          Example: "sentAt>=2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"
        - createdAt: When the message was logged in Affinity (operators: >, <, >=, <=)
          Format: ISO 8601 timestamp
          Example: "createdAt>=2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"
        - updatedAt: When the message was last updated (operators: >, <, >=, <=)
          Format: ISO 8601 timestamp
          Example: "updatedAt<=2025-12-31T23:59:59Z"

        Date range example:
        "sentAt>=2025-01-01T00:00:00Z & sentAt<2025-02-01T00:00:00Z"

        Boolean logic: & (AND), | (OR), () for grouping
        Full filtering spec: https://developer.affinity.co/pages/external-api-v2/filtering

    cursor: Cursor for the next or previous page. Pass the value of
        `pagination.nextCursor` or `pagination.prevCursor` from a prior
        response. Do NOT parse or modify the cursor string.
    limit: Number of items to include in the page. Default is 20, max is 100.

Returns:
    A dict with `data` (list of chat messages) and `pagination` with
    `nextCursor` / `prevCursor` strings (pass directly to the `cursor`
    param; absent when there is no such page) and `nextUrl` / `prevUrl`
    full URLs (null when there is no such page).
    Each chat message has `id`, `sentAt`, `direction` ("sent" or
    "received"), `loggingType` (always "manual"), `creator`, `createdAt`,
    `updatedAt` (can be null), and `participantsPreview` (`data`, a list of
    persons, and `totalCount`).

tools.name: get_emails
tools.description:
Get the emails that the current user can see, with their dates, subjects, direction, and participants.

IMPORTANT: The API never returns email bodies, only metadata. If the user cannot
see the subject of an email, `subject` is "********".

Emails come in id order, which is the order in which Affinity stored them, not
the order of their dates. The first page holds the emails that Affinity stored
first. To get recent emails, filter on `sentAt`.

To get the emails of one company, person, or opportunity, use
get_interactions_for_entity. It returns emails newest first.

Args:
    filter_expr: Filter expression using Affinity query language. Available fields:
        - id: unique identifier for the email (operators: =)
          Example: "id=1" or "(id=1 | id=2)"
        - sentAt: When the email was sent (operators: >, <, >=, <=)
          Format: ISO 8601 timestamp
          Example: "sentAt>=2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"
        - createdAt: When the email was added to Affinity (operators: >, <, >=, <=)
          Format: ISO 8601 timestamp
          Example: "createdAt>=2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"
        - updatedAt: When the email was last updated (operators: >, <, >=, <=)
          Format: ISO 8601 timestamp
          Example: "updatedAt<=2025-12-31T23:59:59Z"

        Date range example:
        "sentAt>=2025-01-01T00:00:00Z & sentAt<2025-02-01T00:00:00Z"

        Boolean logic: & (AND), | (OR), () for grouping
        Full filtering spec: https://developer.affinity.co/pages/external-api-v2/filtering

    cursor: Cursor for the next or previous page. Pass the value of
        `pagination.nextCursor` or `pagination.prevCursor` from a prior
        response. Do NOT parse or modify the cursor string.
    limit: Number of items to include in the page. Default is 20, max is 20.
        To get more emails, page through with `cursor`.

Returns:
    A dict with `data` (list of emails) and `pagination` with
    `nextCursor` / `prevCursor` strings (pass directly to the `cursor`
    param; absent when there is no such page) and `nextUrl` / `prevUrl`
    full URLs (null when there is no such page).
    Each email has `id`, `sentAt`, `subject`, `direction` ("sent" when
    someone in the organization sent it, else "received"), `loggingType`
    (always "automated"), `createdAt`, `updatedAt` (can be null), `from`
    (an attendee), and `toParticipantsPreview` and `ccParticipantsPreview`
    (each with `data`, a list of attendees, and `totalCount`). Each attendee
    has `emailAddress` and `person`, which is null when no person in
    Affinity has that address.

tools.name: get_interactions_for_entity
tools.description:
Get the calls, chat messages, or emails (not meetings) of a specific company, person, or opportunity.

For meetings, use get_meetings_for_entity. The results include only the
interactions that the current user has permission to see.

IMPORTANT: The date range between start_time and end_time cannot exceed 365 days.
A larger range is clamped to the most recent 365 days (start_time moves forward),
and a `warnings` entry in the response states the window that was used. To fetch
older interactions, call again with an earlier end_time. start_time must be
strictly before end_time: an inverted or empty range causes an error, not a clamp.

Args:
    interaction_type: The kind of interaction to get:
        - InteractionType.CALL (1)
        - InteractionType.CHAT_MESSAGE (2)
        - InteractionType.EMAIL (3)
        If unclear which type the user means, ask before calling.
    entity_id: The ID of the company, external person, or opportunity. A person must be an
        external contact or a collaborator: the API rejects an internal person with
        "Person is not an external or collaborator".
    entity_type: What type of entity this ID refers to. Options: 0 = person, 1 = company, 8 = opportunity
    start_time: ISO 8601 timestamp. Only interactions that took place at or after this time
        are returned. Must be before end_time.
        Format: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    end_time: ISO 8601 timestamp. Only interactions that took place before this time are
        returned. Must be after start_time.
        Format: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    direction: Return only chat messages or emails in this direction. When not supplied,
        returns both. Not applicable to calls (omit it for those). Options:
        - ChatMessageDirection.SENT (0): sent by someone in your organization
        - ChatMessageDirection.RECEIVED (1): received by someone in your organization
    internal_person_id: ID of an internal person that took part in the interactions.
        This parameter filters the interactions of the given entity down to those
        in which this internal person took part. Cannot be used to find all of an
        internal person's interactions.
    page_size: Number of results per page. Default is 10, maximum is 100.
    page_token: Token for the next page. Pass the value of "next_page_token" from the
        previous response. If "next_page_token" is null, the response is the last page.
        To answer questions that depend on every interaction in the range, call again
        with each new token until it is null. Do NOT parse or modify the token string.

Returns:
    A dict with `next_page_token` and one list of interactions, newest first by
    the date of the interaction. The key of the list depends on interaction_type:
    - CALL: `events`. Each call has `id`, `v2_id` (the call's id in get_calls),
      `date` and `start_time` (both the time of the call that the user logged),
      `end_time`, `updated_at`, `title` (null when the call has no title or the
      user cannot see it), `type` (1), `attendees` (email addresses),
      `persons`, `manual_creator_id`, `notes` (ids of the notes on the call), and
      `ical_uid`.
    - CHAT_MESSAGE: `chat_messages`. Each message has `id`, `date` (when it was
      sent), `direction` (0 = sent, 1 = received), `type` (2), `persons`,
      `manual_creator_id`, and `notes` (ids of the notes on the message, which
      hold the message text).
    - EMAIL: `emails`. Each email has `id`, `date` (when it was sent), `subject`
      (null when the user cannot see it), `type` (3), `direction` (0 = sent,
      1 = received), `from` (a person, or `{"email": ...}` when no person has
      that address), and `to` and `cc` (the persons that match those addresses,
      without the addresses that match no person). Email bodies are never returned.
    Each person has `id`, `type`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `primary_email`, and
    `emails`. To read the text of a note, use query_notes with filter_expr
    "id=<note id>". If the requested date range exceeded 365 days, a `warnings`
    list describes the clamped window that was used.

ChatMessageDirection.description: Direction of a chat message or email interaction.
ChatMessageDirection.title: ChatMessageDirection

tools.name: get_intro_paths
tools.description:
Find ranked warm intro paths to a person or company: who at your org can
introduce you, directly or through one bridge person, strongest path first.

Each path has one or two edges. One edge is a direct relationship between a
person at your org and the target. Two edges go through a bridge person,
where `edges[0].to` and `edges[1].from` are the same person. Paths combine
your org's interaction history and inferred connections (shared work history,
investor-portfolio relationships).

IMPORTANT: Pass exactly one of `person_id` or `company_id`. Both or neither
raises ValueError before any API call. These are Affinity IDs, not names:
call `search_persons` or `search_companies_top_matches` first to resolve a
name to its ID.

IMPORTANT: Paths are already ranked by the API. Present them in the order
returned, using `rank` and `tier`. Do not re-rank them. The response carries
no absolute path score, and `interactionScore` on an edge is not a path
score.

When the paths cannot be loaded for the target, returns `data` as an
empty list and an `unavailable` message that says what to tell the user.
Without `unavailable`, an empty `data` list means no paths were found.

Args:
    person_id: The ID of the target person. Mutually exclusive with
        `company_id`.
    company_id: The ID of the target company. Ranks paths to any person
        currently at that company, so paths may lead to different people.
        Mutually exclusive with `person_id`.
    cursor: Cursor for the next or previous page. Pass the value of
        `pagination.nextCursor` or `pagination.prevCursor` from a prior
        response. Do NOT parse or modify the cursor string.
    limit: Number of paths per page (1-100). Default is 20. Values outside
        1-100 raise ValueError before any API call.
    total_count: When true, the response pagination object includes the
        total number of paths. Default is false.

Returns:
    JSON object with:
    - data: list of paths, strongest first. Each path has:
      - rank: position among all paths to the target (1 is strongest),
        stable across pages of the same request.
      - tier: "strong", "moderate", or "weak" for the path as a whole.
      - target: the person the path leads to (`id`, `name`, `title`,
        `linkedinUrl`, `currentCompany` with `id` / `name` / `domain`, or
        null).
      - edges: one or two hops. Each edge has `from` and `to` people (`id`,
        `firstName`, `lastName`, `primaryEmailAddress`), its own `tier`, and
        `connectionInfo` with the signals behind it: `interactionScore`,
        `lastInteraction` (`type` of email / chat-message with `sentAt`, or
        meeting / call with `startTime` / `endTime`), `linkedIn`
        (`connectedOn`), `sharedWorkHistory` (`sharedEmployer`,
        `overlapStartDate`, `overlapEndDate`), and `investmentHistory`
        (`inference` with `investingFirm` / `portfolioCompany`, and
        `dealContext` with `fundingEvent`, `investor`, `executive`). Absent
        signals are null or empty lists.
    - pagination: object with `nextCursor` / `prevCursor` strings (pass directly
      to the `cursor` param; absent when there is no such page) and
      `nextUrl` / `prevUrl` full URLs (null when there is no such page);
      totalCount is included only when total_count is true.

tools.name: render_intro_paths_graph
tools.description:
Render ranked warm intro paths from get_intro_paths as an interactive
network-map graph, with an evidence panel for each relationship.

Call this every time you present get_intro_paths results to the user:
first give the paths as text, then call this tool for the same paths.
Do not wait for the user to ask for a map. Also call it when the user
asks to see, map, visualize, or diagram the paths. Do not call it on your
own when get_intro_paths returned no paths, or returned `unavailable`.

Call this only after fetching paths with get_intro_paths. This tool does
not fetch or rank anything itself. It draws exactly the paths it is
given, so pass the same paths already shown to the user in text, in the
same order. Never invent a person, relationship, score, or signal that
get_intro_paths did not return.

Each relationship is drawn by what supports it: one with a `score_pct` as
confirmed and scored (solid line with the number), one with only
`linkedin_connected_on` as a confirmed LinkedIn connection (solid blue
line, no number), and one with only `shared_work_history` /
`investment_history` as inferred (dashed line with its tier word). The
rank 1 path is marked as the recommended path; a later page has none.

Example, one direct path and one path through a bridge contact:
    people = [
        {"id": 10, "name": "Jamie Chen"},
        {"id": 22, "name": "Alex Kim", "title": "CTO", "company": "Globex"},
        {"id": 55, "name": "Jane Doe", "title": "CEO", "company": "Acme"},
    ]
    paths = [
        {"rank": 1, "tier": "strong", "edges": [
            {"from_id": 10, "to_id": 55, "tier": "strong", "score_pct": 85,
             "last_interaction": {"type": 3,
                                  "occurred_at": "2026-08-14T15:04:00Z"}}]},
        {"rank": 2, "tier": "moderate", "edges": [
            {"from_id": 10, "to_id": 22, "tier": "moderate", "score_pct": 55},
            {"from_id": 22, "to_id": 55, "tier": "moderate",
             "shared_work_history": [{"employer": "Globex",
                                      "overlap_start_date": "2018-03-01",
                                      "overlap_end_date": "2020-11-30"}]}]},
    ]

Args:
    people: Everyone the paths reference, each listed once. Every entry
        must appear in at least one path.
    paths: Ranked paths from get_intro_paths, in ascending `rank` order.
        Maximum 5. The tool still accepts an empty list and renders an
        empty state, but only pass one when the user asks for it.
    current_user_id: The caller's own person ID, not the user ID that
        get_current_user returns: match its `user.emailAddress` to a
        `primaryEmailAddress` on the paths' edges and pass that person's
        `id`. Marks them "(You)" and addresses the intro request to the
        next person on the path instead. Omit if unknown.
    target_company: The company name, for a company search only. The map
        names the company in its title and lists the contacts in rank
        order, also when every path reaches one contact. Omit it for a
        person search.

Returns:
    JSON object with `people`, `paths`, `current_user_id` and
    `target_company` (when given), and `generated_at` (server-side UTC
    timestamp) for the MCP App to render. Each returned path also
    carries a computed `recommended` boolean, and each edge a computed
    `kind` ("scored", "linkedin", or "inferred") and `also_linkedin`
    boolean. Text-only clients receive the same object as plain JSON.

InteractionType.description:
Types of interactions.

EMAIL is not a valid value for create_interaction (emails can't be
manually logged that way) - it exists for tools that only need to
describe a past interaction, e.g. render_intro_paths_graph.
InteractionType.title: InteractionType

IntroPathsEdge.description:
One relationship between two people: a single `edges[]` entry of a
get_intro_paths path.

Args:
    from_id: `from.id`.
    to_id: `to.id`.
    tier: The edge's own `tier`: "strong", "moderate", or "weak".
    score_pct: `connectionInfo.interactionScore` converted to 0-100 and
        rounded to the nearest integer. Omit when `interactionScore` is
        null. Never pass a path's rank or tier here.
    last_interaction: From `connectionInfo.lastInteraction`. Omit when
        null.
    linkedin_connected_on: `connectionInfo.linkedIn.connectedOn`, e.g.
        "2021-07-14". Omit when `linkedIn` is null.
    shared_work_history: From `connectionInfo.sharedWorkHistory`. Max 5.
    investment_history: From `connectionInfo.investmentHistory`. Max 5.
IntroPathsEdge.title: IntroPathsEdge

IntroPathsInvestment.description:
One investor-executive signal, from `connectionInfo.investmentHistory[]`.
The edge's `from` person is the investor side, `to` the executive side.

Args:
    portfolio_company: `inference.portfolioCompany.name`.
    investing_firm: `inference.investingFirm.name`, when present.
    funding_series: `dealContext.fundingEvent.series`, e.g. "Series B".
    funding_date: `dealContext.fundingEvent.date`, e.g. "2021-06-01".
    funding_amount: `dealContext.fundingEvent.amount`, copied as-is, e.g.
        15000000. Omit when null.
    funding_currency_code: `dealContext.fundingEvent.currencyCode`, the
        ISO 4217 code for `funding_amount`, e.g. "USD". Omit when null.
IntroPathsInvestment.title: IntroPathsInvestment

IntroPathsLastInteraction.description:
The most recent interaction behind a scored relationship, from the
edge's `connectionInfo.lastInteraction`.

Args:
    type: Options: 0 = meeting (InteractionType.MEETING), 1 = call
        (InteractionType.CALL), 2 = chat message
        (InteractionType.CHAT_MESSAGE), 3 = email (InteractionType.EMAIL),
        for the endpoint's "meeting" / "call" / "chat-message" / "email".
    occurred_at: ISO 8601 timestamp, copied as-is from `sentAt` (email,
        chat message) or `startTime` (meeting, call), e.g.
        "2026-08-14T15:04:00Z".
IntroPathsLastInteraction.title: IntroPathsLastInteraction

IntroPathsPath.description:
One ranked path from get_intro_paths.

Args:
    rank: The path's `rank`, copied as-is.
    tier: The path's `tier`: "strong", "moderate", or "weak".
    edges: The path's `edges`, in order: one edge for a direct path, two
        for a path through a bridge contact.
IntroPathsPath.title: IntroPathsPath

IntroPathsPerson.description:
A node in the intro paths graph: someone at your firm, a bridge
contact, or a target.

Args:
    id: Affinity person ID, from `edges[].from.id` / `edges[].to.id` in
        get_intro_paths.
    name: Display name. Control characters and punctuation outside common
        name characters (letters, digits, spaces, `'.,-`) are stripped.
    title: Job title shown under the name, e.g. the path's
        `target.title`, or `get_person_info`'s
        `affinity-data-current-job-title` field. Omit only if you have
        none.
    company: Employer name shown next to the title, e.g. the path's
        `target.currentCompany.name`.
    linkedin_url: Profile URL, e.g. the path's `target.linkedinUrl`. Must
        be an `https://` URL on `linkedin.com` or `linkedin.cn`.
IntroPathsPerson.title: IntroPathsPerson

IntroPathsSharedWorkHistory.description:
One shared-employer signal, from `connectionInfo.sharedWorkHistory[]`.

Args:
    employer: `sharedEmployer.name`.
    overlap_start_date: `overlapStartDate`, e.g. "2018-03-01".
    overlap_end_date: `overlapEndDate`, e.g. "2021-11-30".
IntroPathsSharedWorkHistory.title: IntroPathsSharedWorkHistory

tools.name: get_opportunities_info
tools.description:
Get opportunities (deals) by id: name, list, and whether each is restricted.

Use this when another tool returned opportunity ids without names, for example
get_reminders, get_entity_files or get_entity_file_metadata. To find a deal by
name, call search_opportunities. Returns no field values.

Args:
    opportunity_ids: 1 to 100 opportunity ids.

Returns:
    `opportunities` holds every requested opportunity the API returned. When
    `isRedacted` is true, the opportunity is restricted and the user is not on its
    allow list. Its name shows as "[Hidden]". Tell the user it exists but is hidden,
    and do not guess its name.
    `missingIds` lists requested ids that returned nothing, for example a deleted id
    or one from another organization.

tools.name: get_suggested_field_updates
tools.description:
Get one set of suggested field updates (SFUs) with all its suggestions.

A set is one Data Update Agent run over a note or meeting. Each suggestion
proposes a new value for one field on a company, person or opportunity.
Use list_suggested_field_updates to find set ids. If the note or meeting id
is known, pass subject_type and subject_id to list only that subject's sets.

IMPORTANT: currentValue is the field's value when the suggestions were
generated. The record may have changed since.

Args:
    suggested_field_update_id (required): The set id, a UUID such as
        "7c9e6679-7425-40de-944b-e07fc1f90ae7".

Returns:
    The set. status "pending" is still generating and has no suggestions;
    "open" waits on the user. A run that found nothing is "done" with no
    suggestions. Show records as "Acme Corp (company 4521)".
    Errors: 404 when the set does not exist, is not this user's, or the user
    has no access to suggested field updates.

tools.name: get_suggested_field_updates_task
tools.description:
Check whether suggested field update (SFU) generation has finished.

Reads the task once. It does not poll. Generation can take several
minutes; read again when the user asks.

Args:
    task_id (required): The task id, a UUID such as
        "7c9e6679-7425-40de-944b-e07fc1f90ae7". It equals the set id.

Returns:
    The task. On "success", call get_suggested_field_updates with
    suggestedFieldUpdate.id. "failed" is final and carries no reason.
    Errors: 404 when the task does not exist, is not this user's, or the
    user has no access to suggested field updates.

tools.name: list_suggested_field_updates
tools.description:
List the user's sets of suggested field updates (SFUs), newest first.

A set is one Data Update Agent run over a note or meeting. Items have counts
but no suggestions: call get_suggested_field_updates with an id for those.

IMPORTANT: Runs that found nothing are not listed. An empty list does not
mean the agent is off; say there are no suggestions, and that the agent may
not be enabled for this user.

IMPORTANT: Sets the user cannot see are removed after the page is read, so a
page can be short or empty while `pagination.nextCursor` is set. Keep
paging until `nextCursor` is null.

Args:
    status: Only sets in this status. "open" sets wait on the user.
        "pending" sets are still generating.
    subject_type: Only sets generated from a "note" or a "meeting".
    subject_id: Only sets for this note or meeting id. Requires
        subject_type, because a note and a meeting can share an id; without
        it, raises ValueError before any API call.
        A note attached to a meeting has its sets under the meeting id.
    created_after: Only sets created at or after this ISO 8601 time, for
        example "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z". Lower bound only.
    limit: Sets per page, 1 to 100. Default 20.
    cursor: Pass `pagination.nextCursor` or `pagination.prevCursor` from a
        prior response, unchanged.

Returns:
    One page of sets. Refer to a set's subject by its label, for example
    "the note 'Met Meredith Becker today...' (note 376)". When "note" is
    set, relay it.
    Errors: 400 for a bad filter or cursor; 404 when the user has no access
    to suggested field updates.

SubjectType.description: What a set of suggested field updates was generated from.
SubjectType.title: SubjectType

SuggestedFieldUpdateStatus.description: Status of a set of suggested field updates.
SuggestedFieldUpdateStatus.title: SuggestedFieldUpdateStatus

tools.name: list_suggested_field_updates_tasks
tools.description:
List the user's suggested field update (SFU) generation tasks, newest first.

Args:
    status: Only tasks in this status.
    limit: Tasks per page, 1 to 100. Default 20.
    cursor: Pass `pagination.nextCursor` or `pagination.prevCursor` from a
        prior response, unchanged.

Returns:
    One page of tasks.
    Errors: 400 for a bad cursor; 404 when the user has no access to
    suggested field updates.

tools.name: data_quality_audit
tools.description: Audit the health of an Affinity CRM and deliver a workbook and a one-page HTML audit summary: what is in place today (Your CRM), every check that was run and what it found (Checks), one row per finding with what to do, who does it and a status to track (Findings), and the reference tabs behind them. Use when a user asks for a "data quality audit" or a "CRM audit", to "audit our CRM", "audit our data", "check data quality", "how healthy is our Affinity data", "clean up our CRM", "data hygiene report", or asks what is wrong with or missing from their lists, fields, companies or people. Also trigger for a single audit by name ("just audit our lists"). Also trigger when an audit request asks to find or merge duplicates: the skill explains that duplicate records are out of scope and points to Duplicate Management. Read-only and recommendation-only: never modifies records and never executes clean-up, even when asked.

tools.name: update_field
tools.description:
Update a field (custom column): its name, description, or required flag.

Works on a list-specific field, or on a global company field. Pass only the
values you want to change.

IMPORTANT:
  - Use the field's `type` from `get_list_fields` or `get_entity_fields`. For
    "list", pass the list_id. For a "global" or "enriched" company field, omit
    list_id.
  - Person fields and global opportunity fields are not supported. A field on an
    opportunity list is a list field, so pass its list_id.
  - Only custom fields can be renamed or get a description. Enriched and native
    company fields (for example "affinity-data-location") accept only is_required.
  - A list field needs the Standard role on the list. The list's Status and
    Owners fields, and any is_required change, need the Admin role on the list.
    A company field needs the org-level "manage global fields" permission.
  - A name that another field already uses returns a 400
    ("<name> is an existing column.").
  - The id that `create_field` returns is the field_id for this tool.

Args:
    field_id: Human-readable field ID, for example "field-1234" or
        "affinity-data-location".
    list_id: ID of the list that owns a list-specific field. Omit it for a global
        company field.
    name: New field name (1 to 255 characters).
    description: New description of the field's purpose (up to 255 characters).
    clear_description: Set to True to remove the field's description. Do not
        combine with description. Defaults to False.
    is_required: Whether a value is required when an entity or list entry is
        created. Omit it to leave the setting unchanged.

Returns:
    None. The API returns 204 No Content on success.

tools.name: apply_suggested_field_updates
tools.description:
Apply suggested field updates (SFUs): accept, edit or reject each pending
suggestion in a set, and write the accepted values to the records.

Confirmation gate: with confirm=false (the default) nothing is written. The
response is a preview: "summary", one "rows" item per pending suggestion
(decision, record, field, current_value, new_value), "warning" and
"next_step". Show the summary and every row in your own message. Call again
with the same arguments and confirm=true only after the user approves.

IMPORTANT: Every pending suggestion needs a decision. A suggestion in none
of accept, reject or edits raises ValueError naming it, before any write.
Ask the user about those; never decide for them. An id in edits is
accepted with that value. reject and edits win over accept_all.

Call get_suggested_field_updates first for the suggestion ids, fields and
value types.

Args:
    suggested_field_update_id (required): The set id, a UUID.
    accept: Suggestion ids to accept as suggested.
    accept_all: true accepts every pending suggestion not in reject or
        edits.
    reject: Suggestion ids to reject. Nothing is written for them.
    edits: {suggestion_id: value} to accept with a different value. The
        value's "type" must equal the suggestion's suggestedValue type.
        Shapes by type, with "type" set to that exact type:
        - text: {"type": "text", "data": "CFO"}
        - number: {"type": "number", "data": 42}
        - datetime: {"type": "datetime", "data": "2026-07-16T00:00:00Z"}
        - dropdown or ranked-dropdown: {"type": "ranked-dropdown", "data":
          {"dropdownOptionId": 2}}
        - dropdown-multi: {"type": "dropdown-multi", "data":
          [{"dropdownOptionId": 2}]}
        - company or person: {"type": "company", "data": {"id": 101}}
        - company-multi or person-multi: {"type": "company-multi", "data":
          [{"id": 101}]}
        - location: {"type": "location", "data": {"city": "Austin",
          "state": "TX", "country": "United States"}}
    confirm: false returns the preview only; true writes.

Returns:
    confirm=true: {"summary", "status", "rows", "next_step"}. summary reads
    "Applied 5, edited 1, rejected 2, failed 1. The set is done." Each row
    has the preview fields plus "status" (accepted, edited, rejected,
    failed), and "error" when failed. "next_step" is present only when a
    row failed: show its error, then offer a direct field update.
    Errors: ValueError for an undecided, unknown or conflicting id, a wrong
    edit type, or a set that is not open, all before any write. 400 when the
    API rejects the decisions. 404 when the set is missing or not this
    user's, or the user has no access to suggested field updates.

tools.name: dismiss_suggested_field_updates
tools.description:
Dismiss suggested field updates (SFUs): reject every pending suggestion
in a set and close it. Nothing is written to the records.

Confirmation gate: with confirm=false (the default) nothing changes. The
response has "total", a "warning" with the fields, and "next_step". Show
the warning. Call again with confirm=true only after the user approves.
To keep some suggestions, use apply_suggested_field_updates instead.

Args:
    suggested_field_update_id (required): The set id, a UUID.
    confirm: false returns the preview only; true dismisses.

Returns:
    confirm=true: {"summary", "status"}, for example "Rejected 3. The set
    is done." Errors: ValueError when the set is not open. 404 when the set
    is missing or not this user's, or the user has no access to suggested
    field updates.

tools.name: suggest_field_updates
tools.description:
Run the Data Update Agent on a note or meeting to get suggested field updates (SFUs).

The agent reads the note or meeting and suggests new values for fields on
the companies, persons and opportunities it mentions. Nothing is written
until the user applies the suggestions.

Find the note or meeting first with the note and meeting tools
(search_notes, get_notes_for_entity, get_meetings_for_entity). If more
than one matches the user's words, show the candidates and ask. Never
guess.

The tool starts generation, then checks it every 5 seconds for up to 20
seconds, and returns within 25 seconds. A meeting note runs as its meeting. While a run for the subject
is still generating, a repeat call waits on that run and starts no second
one. Otherwise each call starts a new run, and the user's previous open
set for the subject becomes done: its undecided suggestions can no longer
be decided.

Args:
    note_id: The note id. Pass exactly one of note_id, meeting_id or
        note_url.
    meeting_id: The meeting id. When picking it from
        get_meetings_for_entity, ALWAYS use the response's `v2_id` field if
        it is present and non-null. Only fall back to `id` when `v2_id` is
        absent.
    note_url: A note link such as "https://<tenant>.affinity.co/notes/123",
        as create_note returns.

Returns:
    The run. On "success", suggestedFieldUpdates holds the set; a set
    that is "done" with no suggestions means the agent found nothing to
    update. On "failed", relay message. On "in-progress", follow
    nextStep: check later with get_suggested_field_updates_task, then
    get_suggested_field_updates.
    Errors: 400 for an empty note or a meeting with no external attendee;
    404 when the note or meeting does not exist or is not readable, or the
    user has no access to suggested field updates; 403 for a token without
    write access.

tools.name: delete_field
tools.description:
Permanently delete a field (custom column) and every value set on it.

Works on a custom field of a list, or on a custom global company field.

Confirmation gate: with confirm=false (the default) nothing is deleted. The
response is a summary (warning, field, records_with_values, list_name for a
list field, next_step). records_with_values is the number of list entries or
companies with a value on the field, or null when Affinity could not count
them. Show the whole warning to the user in your own message, keeping the
field name, the list name and the count. Call again with confirm=true only
after the user approves (or already approved this deletion in the
conversation).

IMPORTANT:
  - Use the field's `type` from `get_list_fields` or `get_entity_fields`. For
    "list", pass the list_id. For a "global" company field, omit list_id.
  - Person fields, global opportunity fields, and enriched or native fields
    are not supported. A field on an opportunity list is a list field, so pass
    its list_id.
  - A list field needs the Admin role on the list. A user with the Standard
    role can delete it only when no list entry has a value on it. A company
    field needs the org-level "manage global fields" permission. Without the
    permission, the confirmed call returns a 403.
  - A list field that Affinity manages, such as a list's Status field, returns
    a 400 ("Field cannot be deleted").
  - To remove one option from a dropdown field, use
    `delete_list_field_dropdown_option`, not this tool.

Args:
    field_id: ID of a custom field, for example "field-1234".
    list_id: ID of the list that owns a list field. Omit it for a global company
        field.
    confirm: false returns the summary only; true performs the deletion.

Returns:
    confirm=false: the summary, nothing deleted.
    confirm=true: {"success": true, "field_id": field_id}. A field or list that
    does not exist returns a 404 ("Resource not found"). A global company field
    with a list_id returns the same 404. Omit list_id for it.
